contentBlocks.text: ਹੁਣ ਇੱਕ ਪੂਰਾ ਪੈਰਾ! (Now a whole paragraph!) Real translation work usually means connected sentences, not just one at a time.

Translate this short English paragraph into Punjabi, sentence by sentence, using this week's vocabulary and word-order skill: 'The big dog goes home. The small girl reads a book. The book is red.' Break it into three separate sentences, translate each one applying Subject-Object-Verb order, then check that your translated paragraph reads naturally as connected Punjabi, not just three disconnected sentences.
You just translated a complete short paragraph — real, connected translation work. Tomorrow we'll review everything about translation from this whole week.

objectives: Translate a short, multi-sentence paragraph from English to Punjabi
Apply word order and gender agreement consistently across multiple sentences
materialsNeeded: This week's earlier worksheets for vocabulary reference
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's translation skills.
2. Break the paragraph into 3 separate sentences together.
3. Have the child translate each sentence, checking gender agreement each time.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: translate the 3 sentences on separate days' pacing if needed, rather than requiring all 3 in one sitting
Ready for more: challenge them to add a 4th original sentence continuing the paragraph's story
All Gurmukhi words/sentences used in this lesson were validated against gurmukhifix's Lexicon before writing
teacherGuide.answerKey: ਵੱਡਾ ਕੁੱਤਾ ਘਰ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਛੋਟੀ ਕੁੜੀ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਪੜ੍ਹਦੀ ਹੈ। ਕਿਤਾਬ ਲਾਲ ਹੈ।
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's 'translation practice' description at the paragraph level, the natural culmination of this week's sentence-level translation skills.
